subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & soft-burst policy for Opsly
messages:
From: Kevin Zhang <kevin.zhang@opsly.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@opsly.ai>, Opsly Procurement <procurement@opsly.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU sizing: expected peak patterns + burst ask

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Opsly is excited to move forward with Redwood Dedicated but we need to lock down how burst/autoscale will work before procurement can sign. A few details from our side: 
- Production peak: ~1.1M tokens/hour for inference (50% generation, 50% embeddings) during 2x seasonal events per month; baseline 250k tokens/hr.
- Spiky internal workflows: nightly batch scoring windows (2–3 hours) and marketing-driven on-demand spikes (10–30 minutes).
- Compliance ask: data must stay in our VPC and we need an ops contact for incident calls.

Questions:
1) How do you recommend sizing dedicated slabs vs. shoulder capacity for this profile?
2) Can we define a soft-burst policy (credit-backed) that guarantees no hard evictions below 99th percentile latency?
3) Do you support prewarm lanes for short 10–30 minute spikes?

Can you share a sample capacity estimate and an ops runbook we can attach to the procurement packet?

- Kevin
Senior SRE, Opsly

Attachments: (none in this email)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Zhang <kevin.zhang@opsly.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@opsly.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing: expected peak patterns + burst ask

Hi Kevin — great to hear Opsly is ready to proceed. Quick answers up front, and we'll follow with a draft estimate and policy doc: 

1) Sizing: recommend a two-slab approach — a baseline reserved slab sized for the 70–75th percentile of sustained load, plus a shoulder slab (brokered reserve) sized to cover predictable nightly batch windows. For your numbers, baseline ~0.6M tokens/hr capacity, shoulder slab ~0.4M tokens/hr.
2) Soft-burst: yes — we offer a credit-backed soft-burst with tiered headroom: guaranteed slab + shoulder + transient soft credits for short spikes. Hard evictions only occur if combined headroom and credits are exhausted. We can set latency-based protections that preferentially route critical requests to reserved lanes.
3) Prewarm lanes: supported. We can open ephemeral prewarm VMs/GPU contexts to reduce cold-start for 10–30 minute spikes; these are charged at a lower pro-rated rate when not used.

I'll attach a preliminary capacity estimate and an ops runbook. Karthik and Ben are looping in to draft the exact thresholds and crediting cadence. Quick ask: Kevin — can you share a 30-day token histogram (15m buckets) so we can validate the baseline assumption?

Thanks,
Michael
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Zhang <kevin.zhang@opsly.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@opsly.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: Opsly soft-burst & autoscale policy (for review)

Folks — dropping a draft policy that maps to Kevin's requirements. Please review and call out SLA/credit implications. I'll include this in the Opsly packet once we agree.

--- Draft Soft-Burst + Autoscale Policy (v0.1) ---
Scope: Applies to Redwood Dedicated customers with reserved slabs and optional shoulder capacity. Opsly-specific parameters to be set post-30d histogram validation.

1) Capacity model
- Reserved slab: guaranteed compute pool (no eviction) sized for baseline.
- Shoulder slab: reserved but lower-priority pool; evictions possible only after credit depletion.
- Soft credits: transient tokens allocated per month (credits are consumed when workloads exceed reserved+shoulder capacity). Credits reset monthly and can be banked up to 20%.

2) Credit tiers and preemption
- Tier A (short spikes): 10% of reserved slab, auto-allocated for windows <= 30 minutes, preemption after 45 minutes.
- Tier B (extended spikes): additional 25% allocated from shoulder, requires ops approval to extend beyond 3 hours.
- Eviction order: soft-burst workloads -> shoulder non-critical jobs -> shoulder critical -> reserved (last).

3) Latency protection
- 99th percentile latency guardrail: if we detect degradation beyond agreed SLO for reserved-critical routes, we automatically spill non-critical workloads to degraded routing or delay non-urgent batches.

4) Prewarm lanes
- Prewarm sessions can be scheduled (cron or on-demand). Opsly can reserve N prewarm slots charged per-minute when active; unused reserved prewarm slots incur a small retention fee.

5) Telemetry & runbook hooks
- Token-level cost/latency dashboards, per-route tracing, and an incident playbook with RTO/RPO expectations.

6) Billing & credits
- Soft credits billed as a monthly add-on; unused credits can roll forward up to 20% or be purchased as one-off. Credits applied before overage billing.

--- end draft ---

Open items: exact numeric multipliers (we need Kevin's histogram), default prewarm slot counts, and precise credit pricing. Ben — can you run a quick sim with the proposed tiers against a 1.1M peak pattern? Lauren — I'll need a short clause for SLA impact and crediting in the contract.

Onward,
Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Runtime Orchestration

Attachments: opsly_softburst_v0.1.md (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Zhang <kevin.zhang@opsly.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Opsly soft-burst & autoscale policy (for review)

Adding simulation notes — ran the draft model against two synthetic traffic traces that mirror Opsly's described behavior (daily baseline + two monthly events + nightly batch). Highlights: 
- With reserved slab = 0.6M tokens/hr and shoulder = 0.4M tokens/hr, Tier A (10% reserved) covers 85% of observed short spikes under 30 minutes.
- For extreme marketing-driven bursts (10x baseline), prewarm lanes reduce 99th p latency by ~45% compared to cold shoulder routing.
- Suggested guardrail: cap Tier A to 12% for Opsly (slightly higher than draft) and keep Tier B at 25% but require an ops ticket for >3 hour stretches.

Operational notes: we should set automated credit alerts at 60% and 85% consumption, with optional auto-top-up rules. Also propose a soft-fallback model to an alternative lower-cost model family when credits exhausted (best-effort quality degradation).

I'll attach the sim outputs; numbers in the estimate workbook will reflect the 12% Tier A recommendation.

- Ben
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Opsly soft-burst & autoscale policy (for review)

Quick legal/contract note: any SLA language referencing "no hard evictions below 99th percentile latency" is risky as written. Recommend instead: "Redwood will maintain reserved-critical route latency targets under normal operating conditions; in event of sustained, abnormal spikes exceeding agreed headroom and credit allowances, Redwood will enact pre-agreed mitigation (prewarm, degraded-routing, or temporary traffic shaping) and provide credits consistent with the contract's overage schedule."

Also, define what counts as "critical" routes (we should get Opsly to mark their top 3 mission-critical endpoints). For procurement, include a one-page runbook excerpt and the credit pricing table. I can draft the contract clause once Ben and Karthik finalize numbers.

— Lauren
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing: expected peak patterns + burst ask

Kevin / Maya — thanks for the prompt details and for reviewing the draft policy. Next steps and deliverables: 
1) Opsly to provide 30-day token histogram in 15m buckets (requested by EOD Tue, Nov 24).
2) Redwood will deliver: a) a capacity estimate workbook (attached), b) an ops runbook excerpt, c) final soft-burst policy with numerical tiers, and d) draft contract clause for crediting/SLA by Fri, Nov 26.
3) Temporary measures: we will provision a set of 6 prewarm slots in the staging shoulder for an initial trial to validate 10–30 minute spike behavior. Trial terms: no charge for the first 72 hours of aggregated prewarm time; subsequent usage billed per-minute.

Action items for Opsly: share the histogram + mark top 3 critical endpoints. For procurement: we'll include the runbook excerpt and SOC snapshot (opsly_soc2_snapshot.pdf) in the packet.

I've attached the preliminary capacity estimate workbook that uses Ben's 12% Tier A recommendation and the shoulder/reserved split noted earlier. Please confirm and we'll lock numbers into the SOW.

Best,
Michael
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
